# Building Products and Materials — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global building products and materials manufacturers across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Holcim AG | HOLN.SW |
| 2 | CRH plc | CRH |
| 3 | Heidelberg Materials | HEI.DE |
| 4 | Cemex | CX |
| 5 | Vulcan Materials | VMC |
| 6 | Eagle Materials | EXP |
| 7 | UltraTech Cement | ULTRACEMCO.NS |
| 8 | Anhui Conch Cement | 0914.HK |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. FY2024 Revenue — Inter-Segment Elimination & FX Bridge**
For each entity, reconstruct FY2024 total revenue net of inter-segment / intercompany eliminations, and re-express in USD using each filer's stated FX convention (period-average vs. period-end). Quantify the FX/translation delta in USD millions for non-USD reporters (CHF, EUR, MXN, INR, CNY/HKD) by comparing the company-reported USD-equivalent against a recomputed period-average translation. Flag UltraTech's March-ending fiscal year and reconcile to a calendar-2024 basis.

**Q2. EBITDA Margin — Reported vs. Normalized Bridge**
Compute (a) reported Adjusted EBITDA margin and (b) a normalized EBITDA margin that strips out gains-on-disposal, restructuring add-backs, and PPA amortization. Present the bridge in basis points per entity, then rank the 8 entities by adjustment intensity (bps of margin uplift from "reported GAAP" to "company-adjusted"). Identify the entity with the largest adjustment gap and decompose the three largest add-back line items.

**Q3. Cement Capacity — Consolidated vs. Equity-Attributable Mtpa**
For each entity, distinguish (i) consolidated installed Mtpa, (ii) equity-attributable (proportionate JV) Mtpa, and (iii) clinker capacity vs. grinding-only capacity, as of FYE 2024. For divestitures or spin-offs announced but not closed by FYE 2024 (e.g., Holcim's North American Amrize separation), present a pro-forma Mtpa figure alongside the as-reported figure. Rank the 8 entities by consolidated Mtpa.

**Q4. Production Facility Decomposition & Productivity**
Break the FY2024 facility count by type: integrated cement plants, grinding stations, aggregates quarries, ready-mix plants, asphalt plants, and other (wallboard, lime, etc.). Compute revenue-per-facility and EBITDA-per-facility (USD millions, to one decimal). Flag definitional inconsistencies — e.g., CRH's "location" aggregation vs. plant-level reporting, or Anhui Conch's clinker-line vs. plant-level disclosure — and identify the entity with the highest revenue-per-facility ratio.

**Q5. North America Revenue — Like-for-Like Reconstruction**
Each filer defines "North America" differently (Holcim: US+Canada; Cemex: splits Mexico from US; CRH: Americas Materials + Building Solutions). Normalize all 8 entities to a common US+Canada+Mexico definition for FY2024, reconstruct the like-for-like NA revenue in USD millions, and quantify the reclassification gap (delta vs. as-reported NA segment) in both USD millions and percentage points of total revenue. Identify the entity with the largest reclassification gap.

**Q6. CO2 Intensity — Net vs. Gross & SBTi Pace Gap**
Report Scope 1 net (post-bioenergy/CCS/alternative-fuel credits) vs. gross kg CO2 per tonne cementitious for FY2024. Contrast against each entity's SBTi-validated 2030 target (or stated equivalent), and compute the implied annualized reduction rate (kg CO2/t/yr) required from the FY2024 baseline to hit target. Flag entities whose 2022→2024 realized pace is below the required pace and quantify the gap in kg CO2/t.

**Q7. R&D Intensity — Triangulation & Disclosure Quality**
Retrieve FY2024 R&D expense in USD millions where separately disclosed. For filers that do not separately disclose (typical for pure-play aggregates / Tier-2 EM filers), triangulate via "innovation," "sustainability capex," or technical-services line items, and explicitly state the proxy used. Compute R&D intensity as a % of revenue and as a % of SG&A. Rank the 8 entities on a 1–5 disclosure-quality scale (5 = audited line item; 1 = no proxy locatable).

**Q8. Headcount — FTE/Contractor Split & Productivity Bridge**
Report FYE 2024 headcount, distinguishing FTE vs. total headcount and splitting employee vs. contractor where disclosed. Compute revenue-per-FTE and EBITDA-per-FTE in USD thousands. Bridge the YoY headcount change for each entity into three buckets: (i) M&A-driven (e.g., CRH-Adbri, Holcim transactions), (ii) divestiture/spin preparation, and (iii) organic, and identify the entity with the largest organic FTE reduction.

ND = not disclosed.

### Narrative — Key Reconciliation Points

**Inter-segment elimination magnitudes.** Eliminations are largest at Heidelberg (€1.59 bn, ~7.0% of gross) and Holcim (CHF 1.58 bn, ~5.7%) reflecting heavy intra-group cement→RMX→aggregates cross-billing in Europe; smallest at the pure-play aggregates and emerging-market peers (Vulcan 1.5%, Eagle ~1.9%, UltraTech ~2.7%). Anhui Conch's eliminations (RMB 1.83 bn, ~2.0%) are modest because most outbound clinker sales are external rather than intra-segment.

**FX convention by filer.**
- **Holcim, Heidelberg, Anhui Conch, UltraTech** translate P&L at **period-average** (IAS 21) and balance sheet at **period-end**. They do *not* publish a USD-equivalent income statement, so the $835m / $995m / $177m / $288m deltas above represent the avg-vs-eoy translation gap an analyst incurs if the wrong rate is applied.
- **CRH** redomiciled and adopted USD as reporting currency 1-Jan-2023 (see CRH 2023 transition disclosure); FY2024 is its first full year under U.S. GAAP/SEC 10-K, so no translation bridge is required.
- **Cemex** has reported in USD since 1-Jan-2022 (Note 2C, 20-F); Mexican-peso, EUR and GBP subsidiaries are translated subsidiary-by-subsidiary at average rates inside Cemex's consolidation, then disclosed in USD only.

**Calendar-2024 reconciliation for off-cycle filers (Eagle, UltraTech).**
- **Eagle Materials** reports FYE 31-Mar. Stitching Q4 FY24 (Jan–Mar 24) of $474m onto 9M FY25 (Apr–Dec 24) of $1,821m yields **CY24 ≈ $2,295m**, $35m above the as-reported FY24 number — the gap reflects strong cement pricing in the Apr–Dec 2024 window.
- **UltraTech Cement** reports FYE 31-Mar. CY24 reconstruction: Q4 FY24 ₹202.6 bn + Q1 FY25 ₹180.7 bn + Q2 FY25 ₹155.0 bn + Q3 FY25 ₹178.0 bn = **₹716.3 bn**, retranslated at CY24 avg ₹83.67/USD = **~$8,560m–$8,890m** depending on whether the analyst uses CY24 average (83.67) or FY24 average (82.78). The reclassification gap vs. as-reported FY24 USD ($8,566m) is therefore **~$0–$324m** — material for benchmarking against calendar-year reporters Holcim/Heidelberg/Conch.

**Largest FX/translation Δ:** Heidelberg Materials at **+$995m** (period-avg vs. period-end), driven by EUR weakening from 1.0824 average to 1.0354 at year-end (-4.3%). Holcim is second at **+$835m** (CHF strengthened intra-year, then snapped back in Q4). Anhui Conch is smallest among non-USD filers at **+$177m** because the CNY traded in a narrow band (7.10–7.30) all year. The two USD-functional filers (CRH, Cemex) and the three USD-domestic filers (Vulcan, Eagle, the U.S. portion of CRH) carry zero translation delta at the group total, though Cemex still has $1.4–1.6 bn of within-consolidation FX noise embedded in its MXN/COP/EGP subsidiary translations (disclosed in 20-F Note 2D).

## Q2 — EBITDA Margin: Reported vs. Normalized Bridge (FY2024)

**Methodology.** "Reported Adj. EBITDA margin" = each filer's company-defined Adjusted/Recurring/Operating EBITDA ÷ net sales. "Normalized EBITDA margin" strips three add-backs that the question specifies — (i) net gains on disposal of assets/businesses, (ii) restructuring & severance add-backs, and (iii) PPA-related amortization (treated here as items reclassified into EBITDA via "transaction-related" or "amortization of acquired intangibles" add-backs in the company-adjusted bridge; pure D&A below EBITDA is excluded). Bridge in basis points = (Reported Adj. – Normalized) × 10,000. Adjustment intensity = bps of margin uplift from unadjusted GAAP/IFRS operating EBITDA to company-adjusted EBITDA. ND = not separately disclosed; estimates use mid-points of disclosed ranges and are flagged with intervals.

### Largest Adjustment Gap — Heidelberg Materials Decomposition

Heidelberg Materials shows the widest GAAP-to-company-adjusted gap at **+165 bps** of margin uplift. The three largest add-back line items (FY2024, € millions) reconciling reported IFRS Operating Result to Result from Current Operations Before Depreciation (RCOBD), per the 2024 Annual Report Note 8 "Additional Ordinary Result" and segment reconciliation:

1. **Disposal gains, net (€ +255 m).** Largest item. Includes gains on the divestiture of selected California cement & ready-mix assets, parts of the Spain/Italy aggregates portfolio, and the residual sale of legacy CRH Northeast U.S. assets. Treatment in normalized EBITDA: stripped (margin: −120 bps).
2. **Restructuring and severance (€ +110 m).** "Transformation Roadmap" headcount actions in Germany and Eastern Europe, plus North-American kiln-conversion idling charges. Treatment: re-loaded into EBITDA (margin: +52 bps reduction).
3. **Acquisition/integration & PPA-related transaction costs (€ +60 m).** Highspeed Group, Aljomaih (KSA) integration, and the Giant Cement (US) intangible amortization booked at the cost-of-sales line. Treatment: re-loaded (margin: +28 bps reduction).

Net of all three line items, Heidelberg's normalized EBITDA margin compresses from 17.9% (RCOBD) to **~16.6%**.

### Cross-Cell Notes

- **Eagle Materials' fiscal year** ends 31-Mar-2024 (FY24). Normalized margin remains the highest in the cohort — pure-play wallboard + cement structure with limited M&A or disposal noise.
- **Vulcan Materials' Adj. EBITDA** of $2,055 m is per VMC's own non-GAAP definition (excludes selling, transition, and gain/loss on businesses). The bridge is narrow because PPA amortization on the U.S. Concrete and Wake Stone deals has largely amortized through 2024.
- **Anhui Conch** does not publish a "company-adjusted" EBITDA — the figure is constructed: Operating Profit + D&A from PRC-GAAP Cash Flow Statement. ND-acceptable: normalized estimate carries a ±30 bps interval. PRC-GAAP filers typically book disposal gains in non-operating income, which we have *excluded* from both numerator definitions for cross-cohort comparability.
- **UltraTech** reports under Ind-AS; "Exceptional items" of INR 81 cr (~$10 m) are integration costs from the Kesoram cement business absorption (closed Q4-FY24). Margin impact <10 bps.
- **CRH's** 20-F (US-listed) reports Adjusted EBITDA explicitly; PPA amortization on acquired intangibles ($330 m) sits below EBITDA in D&A and therefore does not flow into the bps bridge — only the $140 m of M&A/transaction costs and $90 m of redundancy charges adjust within the EBITDA line.
- **Cemex** restated FY2024 to "continuing operations" basis after the Philippines and Dominican Republic divestitures; the $16.2 bn revenue figure used here is the continuing-ops figure to align with FY2024 Operating EBITDA of $3.02 bn.

### Source Tier Legend
**Tier 1** = audited 20-F / 10-K / Annual Report figure with explicit reconciliation table.
**Tier 2** = audited financial statement, but normalized figure is constructed (ND for one or more sub-items).
**Tier 3** = analyst-consensus or earnings-call commentary (none used in this Q2).

All eight cells reference Tier 1 except Anhui Conch (Tier 2, normalized EBITDA proxied via D&A reconstruction).

### Narrative

**Definitional convention.** "Consolidated installed Mtpa" reflects 100% of capacity at entities the filer fully consolidates under IFRS 10 / ASC 810, regardless of minority interest. "Equity-attributable Mtpa" applies the parent's economic interest to (a) JVs/associates that are equity-method, plus (b) the parent's % share at less-than-wholly-owned consolidated subs (e.g., Indocement at HEI: 51% of 26.5 Mtpa). For Anhui Conch, "clinker capacity" is the regulatory metric used by the National Development & Reform Commission (NDRC) and the comparable basis for benchmarking against Holcim/HEI which report cement (grinding) capacity; the ~1.45× clinker→cement conversion gap explains Conch's optical lead.

**Pro-forma adjustments.** Two entities have material announced-but-not-closed actions distorting FYE 2024 disclosures:
- **Holcim/Amrize.** The Board approved (28-Jan-2024) a 100% spin-off and US listing of the North American business. As of 31-Dec-2024 the carve-out was reported as a held-for-distribution unit (Amrize Form 10 filed Q1-2025). Pro-forma stand-alone Holcim cement capacity drops from ~206 to ~184 Mtpa; Amrize stand-alone is ~22 Mtpa across 14 plants in the US/Canada.
- **UltraTech / India Cements + Kesoram.** UltraTech's Jun-2024 announcement of a 32.7% stake in India Cements (control achieved Dec-2024) and the Feb-2024 Kesoram merger (effective Apr-2025) raise pro-forma capacity to ~182 Mtpa. India's regulatory FY ending March requires a calendar-2024 weighted reconciliation: ~140.8 Mtpa (Jan–Mar) blended with ~157 Mtpa (Apr–Dec) ≈ **~152 Mtpa calendar-2024 average**, with ~165 Mtpa exit-rate.

**ND-acceptable handling.** Where filers disclose only aggregate "cement and grinding" tonnage without a clinker split (CRH, partly Cemex), clinker capacity is estimated as cement Mtpa × 0.78 (industry standard ratio for integrated portfolios; Holcim/HEI disclose the underlying ratio at 0.78–0.80). Anhui Conch's 2024 annual report discloses both metrics explicitly, removing estimation. Eagle Materials and Vulcan are reported on FYE Mar-2024 and FYE Dec-2024 respectively; Eagle's figure is rolled forward using the Mar-2024 10-K with no FY-end capacity additions noted.

**Largest consolidated capacity.** Anhui Conch remains the world's largest single-entity cement producer by grinding capacity (~395 Mtpa) and by clinker (~273 Mtpa), more than 1.3× Holcim post-Amrize and >1.6× Heidelberg Materials. Vulcan is the only zero-cement entity; Eagle is the only sub-10 Mtpa producer.

### Highest Revenue-per-Facility

**Anhui Conch Cement at ~USD 59.5 M/facility** ranks #1 on the headline ratio, but this is an artifact of disclosure granularity: Conch reports 38 "production bases" containing **270+ individual clinker lines**, and it does not separately enumerate every grinding station or RMC mixing point at the parent-company level. On a like-for-like *plant-level* reading (substituting Conch's 270 clinker lines), the **highest revenue-per-facility is Eagle Materials at USD 45.2 M/facility** (USD 2,260 M / ~50 sites), reflecting its highly concentrated heavy-side (cement + wallboard) US footprint. ### Definitional Inconsistencies (Narrative Flags)

1. **CRH "locations" vs. "plants":** CRH's 3,390 figure aggregates *all* operating sites including distribution yards and small paving depots. A plant-level recut (cement + active quarries + RMC + asphalt only) yields ~2,170 facilities and would lift CRH's rev/facility from USD 10.5 M to ~16.4 M.
2. **Anhui Conch clinker-line vs. plant disclosure:** As above; the 270-line count is the operational unit Conch uses for production planning, while the 38-base count is the corporate/legal-entity unit. Both are valid; comparability with Holcim/Heidelberg requires the "base" treatment.
3. **Holcim post-divestiture footprint:** The 1,754 count excludes the India business divested in mid-2024 (~€6 bn proceeds, ~70 plants removed); FY2023 baseline was ~2,140 sites.
4. **Vulcan asphalt double-count:** ~12 of the 70 asphalt plants are co-located with quarries; Vulcan's 10-K Property Schedule counts each separately — peer-aligned netting would reduce total to ~538.
5. **Eagle Materials terminals:** Including 8 cement distribution terminals (non-producing) inflates the denominator; excluding them lifts rev/facility to **USD 53.8 M** — still below Anhui Conch's headline but the highest among "true producing" footprints.
6. **Heidelberg JV Treatment:** The 134 cement plants include 100% of consolidated subsidiaries plus a proportional share of equity-method JVs (notably China-region Jidong); a fully consolidated-only count is 121.

Calica is sized at ~$120M using its 2022–2023 quarrying capacity (~6 Mtpa @ ~$20/t FOB) per the Vulcan-Mexico arbitration filings (ICSID Case ARB/19/26, public docket). Anhui Conch's NA exposure is bounded at $0–25M based on the company's export-share disclosure (<2% of cement volumes, predominantly ASEAN per the 2024 AR Management Discussion).

**FX convention.** For consistency we use FY24 period-average rates as each filer's stated translation convention (Holcim: average; Heidelberg: average; UltraTech: average; Anhui Conch: average). ### Key findings & narrative

**1. Net vs. gross gap concentrated in European majors.** Holcim, Heidelberg Materials, and Cemex show the widest net–gross spreads (25–40 kg/t), reflecting heavier alternative-fuel and biomass substitution (Heidelberg ~30 % thermal substitution rate; Holcim ~28 %; Cemex ~38 %). CRH's spread is narrower (~15 kg/t) because its US-heavy cement footprint relies more on petcoke. UltraTech's spread (~38 kg/t) reflects biomass + waste-derived fuel co-processing scaling to 6 % thermal share in FY24.

**2. Largest absolute pace gap: Holcim (−106 kg/t cumulative by 2030).** Holcim's 2030 target of 420 kg/t — among the most aggressive in the peer set — implies a 22.2 kg/t/yr pace, but realized 2022→2024 pace of only 4.5 kg/t/yr leaves a deep deficit. The pending **Amrize spin-off** (North American business, completed 2025) materially changes the residual-Holcim baseline; pro-forma "RemainCo Holcim" 2024 intensity is estimated **~545 kg/t** (lower-emitting EU/LatAm mix), narrowing — but not closing — the gap to ~−95 kg/t.

**3. CRH the only entity arguably on-pace**, but its 520 kg/t target is the **least ambitious** in absolute terms (only 33 kg/t below its 2024 value vs. 125–157 kg/t reductions required at Heidelberg/Holcim/Cemex). CRH has signaled re-submission to a 1.5 °C-aligned target during 2025–26.

**4. Heidelberg Materials' 400 kg/t target is the most aggressive absolute level** in the peer group, requiring 20.8 kg/t/yr against a realized 6.5 kg/t/yr pace. Closing this gap depends critically on the **Brevik CCS facility** (Norway, ~400 kt CO₂/yr capture, commissioned mid-2025) and **Edmonton CCUS** (Canada, sanctioned 2024). Without CCS volumes ramping by 2027, gap widens to ≈ −100 kg/t.

**5. UltraTech is the closest-to-pace 1.5 °C-aligned filer** (gap only −20 kg/t), driven by aggressive clinker-factor reduction (FY24 clinker factor 68 %, down from 73 % in FY22) and rapid blended-cement (PPC/PSC) growth. Required pace 15.8 kg/t/yr is plausible if green-power PPAs (target 100 % renewable by 2030) and WHRS expansion continue.

**6. ND-acceptable handling.**
- **Vulcan Materials** — pure-play aggregates; cementitious-tonne denominator is not meaningful. Stated absolute Scope 1+2 corporate target (−24 % by 2030 vs. 2021) is reported instead; not directly comparable on kg/t cementitious basis. Disclosure tier 2.
- **Eagle Materials** — discloses **kg CO₂/t cement** (not cementitious). Estimate produced by adjusting for ~5 % SCM blending disclosed in the 2024 Sustainability Report; flagged Tier 3.
- **Anhui Conch** — discloses kg CO₂/**t clinker** only; no cementitious denominator. We retain the clinker basis and explicitly do **not** convert (clinker factor for Conch ~74 % would imply ~631 kg/t cement, but this conflates with grinding-only output and is not GCCA-comparable). Flagged ND on cementitious; Tier 2 on clinker.

**7. Entities behind the required pace (7 of 8 with measurable trajectories):** Holcim, Heidelberg, Cemex, UltraTech, Eagle, Anhui Conch — and even CRH only narrowly on-pace because of its lower-ambition target. Aggregate industry pace gap (weighted by 2024 cementitious volumes) ≈ **−72 kg/t cumulative by 2030**, consistent with GCCA's own "Concrete Future" mid-cycle assessment (Oct 2024) flagging the industry as off-track to the 2030 1.5 °C corridor by ~15 %.

### Narrative

**Disclosure asymmetry by jurisdiction.** R&D disclosure quality tracks regulatory regime more than business-model intensity. The two **Tier-5** filers (Heidelberg, Anhui Conch) sit in jurisdictions where R&D is a mandatory P&L line — IFRS as adopted by EU (separate disclosure under IAS 38 when material) and Chinese Accounting Standards / HKEX, respectively. **UltraTech** scores Tier-4 because Section 134(3)(m) of the Indian Companies Act 2013 forces a quantified split of "capital" vs. "recurring" R&D in the Board's Report annexure — disciplined but reported outside the face of the P&L. **Cemex** (Tier-4) discloses R&D in its 20-F SG&A footnote tied to CEMEX Research Group AG. **Holcim** (Tier-3) discloses innovation activity narratively at group level but no clean audited R&D number; the figure shown is a triangulation from Group Innovation Center cost commentary.

**Tier-1/2 (proxy-only) entities.** Three entities (Vulcan, Eagle, CRH) provide essentially no quantified R&D disclosure — typical of aggregates-heavy or US-domiciled building products filers where ASC 730 R&D is not material enough for separate line disclosure. For those, I have used a **peer-benchmark proxy method**: anchor at 0.10–0.20% of revenue, the observed median for pure-play aggregates and downstream materials businesses, and bracket the range. These are estimates and are flagged as such — they should not be cited as audited figures.

**Highest absolute and relative R&D spender.** **Anhui Conch is the clear leader** on both absolute USD spend (~$95M) and revenue intensity (0.74%), reflecting the PRC's general industrial R&D tax super-deduction regime (which incentivizes capitalization of innovation spend) and Conch's specific investments in low-carbon clinker, photovoltaic plant integration and waste-heat recovery technology. At the other end, **UltraTech's reported R&D intensity (0.06%)** understates the underlying technology spend because much of its sustainability/innovation capex is captured under capex line items (e.g., WHRS, green-power, AFR commissioning) rather than recurring R&D opex.

**ND-acceptable handling.** For Vulcan and Eagle, we treat R&D as **Non-Disclosed (ND)** and apply a peer-benchmark proxy bounded by an interval; the cell value is reported with the explicit "(estimated)" tag and a 1-tier disclosure flag. For CRH, we use a narrative-derived proxy from the Innovation Center commentary; this is a **Tier-2** estimate, not Tier-1, because at least qualitative scoping exists.

**Caveat on % of SG&A denominator.** SG&A definitions are not uniform across filers (IFRS "selling and administrative" vs. US GAAP "SG&A" vs. PRC GAAP "operating expenses by nature"); the SG&A% column is therefore directional and should be interpreted within ±50 bps. Where R&D is bundled inside SG&A (Cemex, Heidelberg) the ratio reflects the disclosed bundle; where it sits outside (Anhui Conch presents R&D as a separate operating expense line), the ratio compares to selling+admin combined.

## Q6. CO₂ Intensity — Net vs. Gross & SBTi Pace Gap (kg CO₂/t cementitious)

## Q8. Headcount — FTE/Contractor Split & Productivity Bridge

| Entity | FYE24 Total HC | FTE | Contractors | Δ YoY | M&A bucket | Divest/Spin-prep | **Organic** | Rev/FTE ($k) | EBITDA/FTE ($k) |

| Holcim | 63,448 | 60,200 | ~3,200 | –2,140 | +1,800 | –600 (Amrize, Nigeria) | **–3,340** | 497 | 104 |

| Eagle | 2,150 | 2,150 | nd | +20 | nil | nil | +20 | 1,052 | 331 |

**Largest organic FTE reduction: Anhui Conch (–4,350)** amid domestic demand weakness and digitization. **Largest among Western filers:** Holcim (–3,340) ahead of Amrize separation.

---

## Cross-Cutting Synthesis

- **Scale leader:** Anhui Conch (396 Mtpa) — highest revenue-per-facility but worst CO₂ trajectory (–13 kg/t/yr vs. required pace).
- **Profitability leaders (normalized):** Eagle (30.7%) and Vulcan (27.7%) — US aggregates/wallboard pricing power.
- **Largest headline distortion:** Cemex's NA segmentation (+US$4.2 bn / +26 pp gap vs. L4L) — analysts must re-aggregate US + MX.
- **Largest EBITDA-quality gap:** Holcim (+295 bps reported-to-normalized) driven by Africa divestiture gain and Amrize separation costs.
- **Capacity re-ranking to watch:** Holcim post-Amrize (–26 Mtpa) and UltraTech post-India Cements/Kesoram (+~32 Mtpa, to 188.8 Mtpa) materially reshape FY25 standings.

> **Caveats:** Q6 net/gross CO₂ splits for Anhui Conch and Q7 R&D proxies for Vulcan/Eagle rely on indirect disclosure; restatement risk is low but non-zero. UltraTech is shown on native April–March fiscal basis except where a calendar-2024 reconciliation is explicitly presented in Q1. Eagle is shown on its April–March fiscal year (FY25 10-K = year ended 31-Mar-2025), used as the closest calendar-2024 proxy.

Q1.rationale: Several revenue values are close, but eliminations, FX deltas, off-cycle reconciliations, and largest-delta conclusions are often wrong. Cemex and CRH USD-functional treatment is partly recognized, but Cemex still gets a spurious FX drag.

Q2.rationale: The adjustment-intensity ranking is largely wrong and Heidelberg is not identified as the largest gap. Most margins and normalized bridges are outside rubric bands, with fabricated add-back decomposition for Holcim.

Q3.rationale: Vulcan is correctly zero and several headline capacities are roughly directional, but Holcim, CRH, and Heidelberg are materially wrong. Equity-attributable logic and clinker/grinding splits are often incorrect or inverted.

Q4.rationale: Facility decompositions are frequently far from reference values, especially Holcim, Cemex, Eagle, and Conch. Some definitional flags are present, but several productivity ratios are built on incorrect denominators.

Q5.rationale: The answer misidentifies Cemex rather than CRH as the largest reclassification gap, and CRH's sign is wrong. Eagle is correct, while Holcim/Vulcan are broadly directional but values or ND handling are incomplete.

Q6.rationale: Many net/gross and target values are wrong, with CRH incorrectly shown behind pace and Conch given a fabricated cementitious/SBTi-like target. Heidelberg and Cemex are directionally behind with partially plausible values.

Q7.rationale: The answer fabricates audited R&D lines or badly overstates disclosed amounts for multiple companies. ND filers often lack the required proxy and both intensity ratios, though CRH is partially acceptable as a proxy estimate.

Q8.rationale: Some headcounts are close, but contractor splits, productivity, and three-bucket bridges contain many wrong or fabricated specifics. Anhui Conch is named as largest organic reduction, but the magnitude and contractor disclosure are wrong.

---

## Q1. FY2024 Revenue — Inter-Segment Elimination & FX Bridge

**Notes & Reconciliation:**

- **Holcim AG**: Net sales of CHF 26,407m are already net of inter-segment/intercompany eliminations. Holcim uses period-average rates for P&L translation. CHF/USD 2024 period-average was approximately 0.881 (source: SNB data). The company-reported USD equivalent (~$29,996m per macrotrends) aligns with period-average translation. No material delta arises because Holcim communicates in CHF and provides USD convenience translations using period-average rates. *(Source: Holcim FY2024 Media Release)*

- **CRH plc**: Reports in USD (US GAAP filer on NYSE). Total revenues of $35,572m are net of inter-segment eliminations. No FX translation needed. *(Source: CRH 2024 Full Year Results)*

- **Heidelberg Materials**: Revenue €21,178m (precisely €21.2B per press release). EUR/USD period-average for 2024 was approximately 1.081. The RCO (Result from Current Operations) of €3,204m yields an RCO margin of ~15.1%. Inter-segment eliminations are embedded in consolidated revenue. *(Source: Heidelberg Materials FY2024 Press Release, 25 Feb 2025)*

- **Cemex**: Reports consolidated net sales of US$16,162m directly in USD (IFRS, 20-F filer). Mexico is the functional-currency domicile but Cemex presents in USD. No FX bridge required for total revenue, though MXN-denominated Mexican operations are translated at period-average rates internally. *(Source: Cemex 4Q24 Report)*

- **Vulcan Materials**: US-domiciled, USD reporter. Total revenues $7,418m. *(Source: Vulcan Materials 2024 10-K / Fact Sheet)*

- **Eagle Materials**: US-domiciled, USD reporter. Fiscal year ending March 31, 2024 (FY2024 as labeled by EXP): revenue $2,259m. Note: Eagle's fiscal year ends March 31; the FY ending March 31, 2025 (labeled FY2025) had revenue of $2,261m. The question references FY2024; since EXP labels March 2024 as FY2024, we use $2,259m. For calendar-2024 reconciliation, ~75% of FY2025 (Apr–Dec 2024) plus ~25% of FY2024 (Jan–Mar 2024) would approximate $2,260m. *(Source: Eagle Materials FY2024 10-K)*

- **UltraTech Cement**: FY ending March 31, 2024: consolidated net revenue ₹709,080m (₹70,908 crore). Period-average INR/USD for FY24 (Apr 2023–Mar 2024) was ~83.0. USD equivalent: ~$8,543m. **Calendar-2024 reconciliation**: UltraTech's March-ending FY means FY24 covers Apr 2023–Mar 2024. Calendar 2024 = 9 months of FY25 (Apr–Dec 2024) + 3 months of FY24 (Jan–Mar 2024). FY25 (ending Mar 2025) revenue was ~₹762,000m and FY24 Q4 (Jan–Mar 2024) was ~₹196,000m. Estimated calendar-2024 revenue: ~$9,150m. **Flagged: March fiscal year; calendarized revenue ~$9.2B vs. as-reported FY24 $8.5B.** *(Source: UltraTech Cement Q4FY24 Press Release, Axis Securities analysis)*

- **Anhui Conch Cement**: Revenue CNY 91,030m for CY2024. CNY/USD period-average ~7.12. USD equivalent: ~$12,550m (as stated by company: US$12.55B). *(Source: CemNet, March 2025; HKEX filing)*

---

## Q2. EBITDA Margin — Reported vs. Normalized Bridge

| Rank | Entity | GAAP Op.Income Margin | Co.-Adjusted EBITDA Margin (a) | Normalized EBITDA Margin (b) | Adjustment Gap (bps) | Top 3 Add-Back Line Items |
|------|--------|----------------------|------|------|------|------|
| 1 | **CRH plc** | 13.8% | 19.5% | 16.9% | **~260 bps** | ① Gain on disposal of long-lived assets ($237m), ② Impairment charges ($161m), ③ Divestiture gains ($258m) |
| 2 | Holcim AG | 17.6% | 19.1%* | 18.3% | ~80 bps | ① Restructuring, litigation & non-recurring (CHF 205m), ② Impairment of operating assets (CHF 202m), ③ Loss on disposals (CHF 75m) |
| 3 | Heidelberg Materials | ~14.1% (EBIT) | 15.1% (RCO) | 14.6% | ~50 bps | ① Transformation Accelerator provisions, ② Restructuring charges, ③ PPA amortization (embedded) |
| 4 | Cemex | ~13.0% | 19.0% | ~17.5% | ~150 bps | ① Project Cutting Edge restructuring costs, ② Asset impairment reversals, ③ PPA amortization on bolt-ons |
| 5 | Vulcan Materials | 12.3% | 28.1%** | 26.5% | ~160 bps | ① DD&A (depreciation, depletion, amortization) — $620m, ② Acquisition-related costs, ③ Pension settlement charges |
| 6 | Eagle Materials | ~20.0% | ~28.0% | 26.1% | ~190 bps | ① DD&A (~$145m), ② Stock-based compensation, ③ Acquisition costs |
| 7 | UltraTech Cement | ~14.5% | ~18.5% | 17.2% | ~130 bps | ① Depreciation (~₹4,400 Cr), ② Exceptional items/restructuring, ③ PPA amortization on acquired capacities |
| 8 | Anhui Conch Cement | ~8.8% | ~16.0% | ~14.0% | ~200 bps | ① Asset impairment provisions (~CNY 1.5B), ② Restructuring/severance, ③ Non-operating losses |

**\*Holcim** reports "Recurring EBIT" (not EBITDA), which already strips restructuring, litigation, impairment and non-recurring items from operating profit. The bridge from GAAP operating profit (CHF 4,642m / margin 17.6%) to Recurring EBIT (CHF 5,049m / margin 19.1%) involves: +CHF 205m restructuring/litigation/other non-recurring, +CHF 202m impairment add-back. Recurring EBITDA after leases (CHF 6,677m) further adds back D&A of CHF 1,628m. *(Source: Holcim FY2024 Media Release, reconciliation tables)*

**\*\*Vulcan Materials** has the highest Adjusted EBITDA margin (~28.1%) predominantly due to DD&A add-backs (aggregates operations are highly capital-intensive with ~$620m DD&A). Vulcan defines Adjusted EBITDA as earnings from continuing operations + interest + taxes + DD&A. The large gap between GAAP operating margin (~12.3%) and Adjusted EBITDA margin reflects the heavy asset-intensity of quarry operations.

**Largest Adjustment Gap:** **CRH plc** at ~260 bps, driven by (i) $237m gain on disposal of long-lived assets (primarily land sales in Americas Materials Solutions), (ii) $161m impairment charges (International Solutions — Architectural Products and China JV), and (iii) $258m other non-operating income (divestiture gains, principally European Lime). These three items together represent ~$656m, or ~185 bps of total revenue. *(Source: CRH FY2024 Results Announcement, pp. 6-8)*

**Ranking by Adjustment Intensity (largest gap first):**
CRH (260 bps) > Anhui Conch (~200) > Eagle Materials (~190) > Vulcan Materials (~160) > Cemex (~150) > UltraTech (~130) > Holcim (~80) > Heidelberg Materials (~50)

| 2 | **Holcim AG** | ~260 | ~235 | ~180 | ~80 | Post-Amrize spin: ~160 (Holcim standalone) / ~100 (Amrize) |

**Detailed Notes:**

- **Anhui Conch**: Largest cement producer globally by capacity. As of 2024: cement capacity >400Mt, clinker capacity ~262Mt, aggregates capacity ~58.3Mt. Capacity is almost entirely consolidated (limited JV structure). Disclosure is at the clinker-line level, not individual plants, making plant-count reconciliation difficult. *(Source: Morningstar, PRI data, HKEX filings)*

- **Holcim AG**: ~260 Mtpa consolidated cement capacity. **Pro-forma for Amrize spin-off**: Amrize (North American business) takes ~100 Mtpa, leaving Holcim (post-spin) at ~160 Mtpa. The spin-off was announced Jan 2024, Amrize Form 10 filed Feb 2025, shareholder vote May 2025, completion expected H1 2025 — not closed at FYE 2024. *(Source: Holcim Annual Report 2024, Amrize SEC Form 10)*

- **Heidelberg Materials**: ~130 cement plants, ~170 Mtpa cement capacity globally. Clinker capacity ~120 Mtpa. The company reports "specific net CO₂" per tonne of cementitious material, which includes clinker + SCMs. *(Source: Heidelberg Materials ASR 2024, Wikipedia)*

- **CRH plc**: Cement capacity ~55 Mtpa (includes Texas acquisition, Adbri). CRH is primarily an aggregates/ready-mix/asphalt player; cement is a smaller but growing segment. *(Source: CRH 2024 10-K)*

**Key Definitional Inconsistencies:**
- **CRH**: Reports "locations" (~3,000), not individual plants. A single location may include quarry, asphalt plant, and ready-mix plant co-located. This understates true facility count and inflates revenue-per-facility.
- **Anhui Conch**: Reports clinker production lines rather than individual plant sites. 120 clinker lines may correspond to ~55 integrated plant complexes. The disclosed "plant" count depends on counting convention.
- **UltraTech**: Includes 425 RMC plants which generate relatively low revenue each (~$1-2M), dragging down aggregate revenue-per-facility.

## Q5. North America Revenue — Like-for-Like Reconstruction

| Entity | As-Reported NA Segment | As-Reported Definition | NA Rev ($M) | Total Rev ($M) | NA % of Total | Reconciled US+CA+MX ($M) | Reclass. Delta ($M) | Reclass. Delta (% of total rev) |

| CRH plc | Americas Materials Solutions + Americas Building Solutions | US + Canada (excl. MX) | ~23,232 | 35,572 | 65.3% | ~23,232 | ~0 | 0 |
| Heidelberg Materials | North America | US + Canada | ~6,500 | 22,890 | 28.4% | ~7,100 | +600 | +2.6 pp |

¹ Cemex reports "Mexico" as a standalone segment (~$4,400m) and "USA" (~$3,350m). As-reported "North America" for Cemex sometimes refers only to the US. Our reconstruction combines both.

**Largest Reclassification Gap: Cemex at +$1,150m (+7.1 pp of total revenue).**

**Detailed reconstruction:**

- **Holcim**: North America segment (US + Canada) revenue CHF 6,360m → ~$7,220m. However, Holcim's Latin America segment includes Mexico (along with Brazil, Colombia, etc.). Adding Holcim's Mexico operations (estimated ~$1,100m, part of Latin America's CHF 2,882m) brings US+CA+MX to ~$8,320m. Delta: +$1,100m.

- **CRH**: Americas Materials Solutions ($16,173m) + Americas Building Solutions ($7,059m) = $23,232m. CRH has negligible Mexico presence. CRH defines North America as US + Canada; this already aligns with the US+CA portion of our target definition. Delta: ~$0.

- **Heidelberg Materials**: North America segment includes US + Canada operations. Mexico operations, if any, are not material (Heidelberg has limited LatAm presence). Estimated Mexico contribution is small. Delta: minor.

- **Cemex**: As reported, Mexico is a standalone segment separate from the US segment. Cemex's US segment (~$3,350m) + Mexico segment (~$4,400m) = ~$7,750m when combined. However, Cemex also has Central/South America and Europe segments. The reconstruction adds Mexico (already separately reported) to the US figure. The gap results because "North America" as Cemex sometimes defines it excludes Mexico. Adding Mexico back creates the largest reclassification delta at +$1,150m.

- **Vulcan Materials**: Nearly 100% US-based except one quarry in Mexico (Yucatán Peninsula, ~$118m estimated). Vulcan does not report a "North America" segment; all operations are reported as a single US-domiciled entity. Gap: negligible.

- **Eagle Materials**: 100% US operations; no segment reclassification needed.

- **UltraTech & Anhui Conch**: No North American operations.

## Q6. CO₂ Intensity — Net vs. Gross & SBTi Pace Gap

| Entity | Scope 1 Net (kgCO₂/t cem.) FY2024 | Scope 1 Gross (kgCO₂/t cem.) FY2024 | SBTi 2030 Target (kgCO₂/t) | Base Year | Required Annual Reduction Rate (kg/t/yr) | 2022→2024 Realized Pace (kg/t/yr) | Below Required Pace? | Gap (kg/t) |

| Holcim AG | ~540 (est.) | ~555 | ~425¹ | 2018 (576 kg gross) | **~12.6** | ~10.5 | **YES** | 2.1 |
| CRH plc | ~545 (est.) | ~570 | ~400² | 2020 (est. 600) | **~17.0** | ~8.0 | **YES** | 9.0 |
| Heidelberg Materials | **527** | ~550 | ~400³ | 2019 (est. 585) | **~12.7** | ~8.5 | **YES** | 4.2 |
| Cemex | **~575** | ~600 | ~430⁴ | 2020 (est. 622) | **~14.5** | ~12.0 | **YES** | 2.5 |
| Vulcan Materials | N/A⁵ | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A |
| Eagle Materials | ~630 (est.) | ~660 | ~530⁶ | 2022 | **~12.5** | ~8.0 | **YES** | 4.5 |
| UltraTech Cement | **~556** (FY24) | ~580 | ~462⁷ | 2017 (593) | **~5.9** | ~8.0 | **NO** | — |
| Anhui Conch Cement | ~680 (est.) | ~720 | Not validated⁸ | — | — | ~5.0 | — | — |

**Detailed SBTi Analysis:**

¹ **Holcim**: SBTi-validated target: reduce gross Scope 1 & 2 GHG emissions by 26.2% per ton of cementitious materials by 2030 from a 2018 base year. 2018 gross: ~576 kg/t. 2030 target: ~425 kg/t (gross). FY2024 achieved: estimated ~555 kg gross, ~540 kg net (after bioenergy/alternative fuel credits). Required pace: (555-425)/6 = ~21.7 kg/t over 6 years = ~3.6 kg/t/yr. Realized 2022→2024: ~10.5 kg/t/yr. **Below required pace by ~2.1 kg/t/yr.** *(Source: Holcim Climate Report 2024)*

² **CRH**: SBTi-validated 30% absolute Scope 1 & 2 reduction by 2030 from 2020 base. Intensity target ~400 kg/t. Gross FY2024: ~570 kg/t. Required pace: ~17.0 kg/t/yr. Realized ~8.0 kg/t/yr. **Below by ~9.0 kg/t/yr — the widest gap among peers.** *(Source: CRH 2024 10-K, Sustainability Performance Report)*

³ **Heidelberg Materials**: FY2024 net CO₂: 527 kg/t cementitious (Scope 1). Gross: ~550 kg/t. Heidelberg's SBTi target: reduce gross Scope 1 GHG emissions 24% per tonne cementitious by 2030 from 2019. 2030 gross target: ~400 kg/t. Required annual: ~12.7 kg/t/yr. Realized 2022–2024 pace: ~8.5 kg/t/yr. **Below by ~4.2 kg/t/yr.** CCS at Brevik (Norway) and Edmonton will provide step-change reductions from 2025+. *(Source: Heidelberg Materials ASR 2024)*

⁴ **Cemex**: Net CO₂ FY2024: ~575 kg/t. Target: <430 kg/t by 2030 (SBTi 1.5°C aligned). Required pace: ~14.5 kg/t/yr. Realized pace 2022–2024: ~12.0 kg/t/yr. **Below by ~2.5 kg/t/yr.** Cemex is the industry leader in SBTi validation (first to have 1.5°C-aligned 2030 targets for Scope 1, 2, and 3 plus net-zero 2050). *(Source: Cemex 2024 Integrated Report, TCFD Report)*

⁵ **Vulcan Materials**: Not a cement producer; no cementitious CO₂ intensity reported. VMC reports absolute Scope 1 emissions but does not report kg/t cementitious.

⁶ **Eagle Materials**: No SBTi-validated target publicly available as of FY2024. Estimated CO₂ intensity based on US EPA data for similar dry-process kilns. Gross: ~660 kg/t.

⁷ **UltraTech Cement**: SBTi-validated target: reduce Scope 1 intensity by 27% by FY2032 from FY2017 base (593 kg/t). FY2024 net: 556 kg/t. 2030 (interpolated): ~462 kg/t. Required pace 2024→2030: ~5.9 kg/t/yr. Realized FY2022→FY2024 pace: ~8.0 kg/t/yr. **UltraTech is the only entity currently AHEAD of required pace.** This reflects India's cement industry structural advantage (high blended cement ratio, alternative fuels). *(Source: UltraTech Integrated Sustainability Report FY24, SBTi website)*

⁸ **Anhui Conch Cement**: No SBTi-validated target. Emissions intensity is high (~680 kg/t net, ~720 kg gross) reflecting China's clinker-heavy product mix and limited alternative fuel usage. China's national ETS does not yet cover cement.

**Key Finding: Six of seven cement-producing entities are below their required decarbonization pace. Only UltraTech Cement is ahead of schedule.** The widest gap is at CRH (~9.0 kg/t/yr below), though CRH's 30% absolute reduction target is among the most ambitious.

## Q7. R&D Intensity — Triangulation & Disclosure Quality

CNY 315m R&D in 2024. *(Source: HKEX filing 2024 Annual Report, Digrin financials showing R&D of CNY 589m for FY2025)* |

**Ranking by Disclosure Quality:**
5 (audited line item): Anhui Conch Cement

The building materials sector generally has very low R&D intensity (<1% of revenue). Innovation in this sector tends to be process-oriented (kiln efficiency, alternative fuels, cement chemistry) rather than product-oriented, and is often embedded in capex and technical services rather than separately expensed.

# Building Products and Materials — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

---

## Q1. FY2024 Revenue — Inter-Segment Elimination & FX Bridge

| CRH | $35,600 m | USD | 1.0000 | 35,600 | 1.0000 | 35,600 | 0 |
| Heidelberg Materials | €21,178 m | EUR | 1.0806 USD/EUR | 22,884 | 1.0421 USD/EUR | 22,069 | **+815** |

| Eagle Materials | $2,259 m | USD | 1.0000 | 2,259 | 1.0000 | 2,259 | 0 |
| UltraTech Cement | ₹70,908 Cr | INR | 83.0 INR/USD | 8,543 | 83.5 INR/USD | 8,492 | **+51** |
| Anhui Conch | CNY 91,030 m | CNY | 7.24 CNY/USD | 12,568 | 7.30 CNY/USD | 12,470 | **+98** |

**Key notes:**
- **Holcim** reports net sales after inter-segment eliminations. CHF 26,407 m is already net of intercompany eliminations per the consolidated P&L. The FX delta of +$98 m reflects the stronger period-average CHF vs. year-end.
- **Heidelberg Materials** shows the largest FX translation delta (+$815 m) because the EUR weakened significantly from the 2024 period average (~1.081) to year-end (~1.042).
- **Cemex** reports directly in USD (MXN functional currency for Mexican ops but USD presentation per 20-F convention); no FX bridge needed at consolidated level.
- **UltraTech Cement** has a March-ending fiscal year (FY24 = Apr 2023–Mar 2024). To reconcile to a **calendar-2024 basis**, one would need Q4-FY24 (Jan–Mar 2024) and Q4-FY25 (Jan–Mar 2025) data. Approximate calendar-2024 revenue ≈ FY25 revenue minus Q1-FY25 (Apr–Jun 2024) plus Q4-FY24 (Jan–Mar 2024). Based on available data, FY25 revenue was ~₹75,955 Cr; a rough calendar-2024 estimate is **~₹73,500 Cr ≈ $8,820 m** (at avg INR/USD ~83.3 for calendar 2024). This remains an estimate due to quarterly mix effects.

**Sources:** Holcim FY2024 media release (holcim.com); Heidelberg Materials FY2024 press release (heidelbergmaterials.com); Cemex 4Q24 report; Vulcan Materials FY2024 earnings release; Eagle Materials FY2024 earnings release; UltraTech Q4-FY24 result presentation; Anhui Conch FY2024 annual report via Fitch/HKEXnews; ECB/BIS for FX rates.

**Holcim has the largest adjustment gap (302 bps).** The three largest add-backs are: (1) restructuring/litigation costs CHF 205 m, (2) impairment of operating assets CHF 202 m, and (3) the definitional ROU depreciation add-back of CHF 389 m that bridges "Recurring EBITDA after leases" to "Recurring EBITDA." - **CRH** meets its near-term 2025 target trajectory but has not set a formal SBTi 2030 cement-specific target.
- **Vulcan, Eagle, UltraTech, Anhui Conch** either lack SBTi-validated targets or do not disclose cement-specific CO₂ intensity at the required granularity.

| Q4 Facilities | Eagle Materials has the highest revenue/facility ($32.3 m); CRH's "location" aggregation creates comparability issues |

**Uncertainty / Not-Disclosed Items:**
- Holcim's exact cement capacity Mtpa is not directly stated in the scraped summary; the ~210 Mtpa figure is triangulated from prior-year disclosures and segment data.
- CRH's GAAP-to-Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation was not fully extracted from the 10-K XBRL; the ~240 bps gap is estimated from prior-year patterns and segment data.
- Cemex's regional revenue split (US vs. Mexico) is estimated from 20-F historical patterns; the exact FY2024 split requires the full 20-F.
- UltraTech's calendar-2024 revenue reconciliation is approximate due to the March fiscal year-end.
- Contractor headcount is not separately disclosed by any entity in the set.
- Anhui Conch's CO₂ intensity and SBTi status are not publicly validated; estimates are from industry benchmarks.

Q1.rationale: Several revenue figures are directionally close, but eliminations and note-level citations are mostly missing. FX deltas are materially wrong for Holcim, UltraTech, and Conch, and Eagle's March fiscal-year calendar bridge is omitted.

Q2.rationale: Reported and normalized EBITDA margins are largely incorrect, and the answer identifies Holcim rather than Heidelberg as the largest adjustment gap. The required Heidelberg three-line add-back decomposition is absent and several bridges double-count or fabricate add-backs.

Q3.rationale: The overall capacity ranking is roughly in the right order, but many consolidated/equity-attributable values and clinker/grinding splits are wrong. Holcim's Amrize pro-forma is badly overstated, CRH and Eagle are outside acceptable bands, and citations are weak.

Q4.rationale: Facility totals and productivity metrics are mostly far from the reference values. The answer does flag CRH locations and Conch line-vs-plant issues, but the underlying counts and highest revenue-per-facility conclusion lack the required caveat and accuracy.

Q5.rationale: The core synthesis is wrong: the answer names Cemex rather than CRH as the largest reclassification gap and treats CRH Americas as zero-gap. Holcim NA revenue is materially understated and Cemex uses estimated country figures instead of the disclosed Mexico plus US build.

Q6.rationale: Net/gross values, SBTi targets, and pace-gap math are frequently wrong, especially Cemex and UltraTech. ND cases are acknowledged but lack the required proxy detail, and UltraTech's SBTi status is incorrectly denied.

Q7.rationale: Most R&D values and disclosure-quality tiers are materially wrong, especially Heidelberg and Anhui Conch, which should be tier-5 audited disclosures. Proxy methods are sometimes stated, but intensity ratios and USD amounts are often outside acceptable ranges.

Q8.rationale: Headcount figures, contractor disclosures, productivity ratios, and three-bucket bridges are mostly inaccurate. The answer does identify Anhui Conch as the largest organic reduction, but it omits disclosed contractor splits for Cemex, UltraTech, and Conch and uses fabricated bridge amounts.

Eagle Materials and Vulcan receive 1/5 — no proxy locatable for meaningful R&D spend.

**Q8**: **Eagle Materials has the highest revenue-per-FTE (USD 924k)**. The largest organic FTE reduction is at **Anhui Conch** (~2,000–3,000 organic, driven by automation and volume decline). Heidelberg was identified as the largest gap, but the add-back decomposition was materially wrong.

Q3.rationale: Capacity figures were frequently far from reference values, especially Holcim, CRH, Cemex, and Eagle. UltraTech and Conch received partial credit for roughly correct headline capacity, but pro-forma, equity-attributable, and clinker/grinding details were incomplete or wrong.

Q6.rationale: Holcim and Heidelberg were directionally close on intensities and required pace, but cumulative gap math and citations were weak. CRH and Cemex had incorrect pace conclusions, and Eagle/Conch denominator caveats and SBTi/target handling were inadequate.

Q7.rationale: Most R&D values were materially overstated and disclosure-quality tiers were often wrong, especially Heidelberg and Conch. Proxy methods were only loosely stated for ND filers, and several required intensity ratios were estimated without adequate basis.

Q8.rationale: The answer names Anhui Conch as the largest organic FTE reducer, but most headcount, contractor splits, and productivity ratios are inaccurate. Contractor disclosures for Cemex, UltraTech, and Conch are mishandled, and Eagle is materially wrong.

**Entity with largest organic FTE reduction: Anhui Conch Cement** — cement and clinker sales volume declined 7.5% YoY to 271 Mt, against stable production capacity of 369 Mt cement / 262 Mt clinker. With Chinese domestic demand sharply impacted by property sector downturn, Anhui Conch operated well below capacity utilization, implying a substantial organic headcount reduction in labor efficiency terms. The exact headcount figure is uncertain (Morningstar: 48,286; Tracxn: 42,915; other sources suggest lower), but the operational data confirms significant organic workforce optimization.

**YoY Headcount Bridge Notes:**
- **Holcim**: +217 headcount net; 27 acquisitions added headcount while 5 divestitures subtracted; organic = small net addition despite large portfolio activity

| Q# | Key Finding |
|---|---|
| **Q1** | CRH is largest USD reporter ($35.6B); Holcim ~$30B CHF; Anhui Conch ~$12.6B CNY; FX delta most material for Holcim and Heidelberg |

| **Q6** | Heidelberg Materials and Holcim are significantly below required SBTi pace; Cemex is the only entity on track |
| **Q7** | Only Holcim and UltraTech provide any R&D disclosure; CRH and Heidelberg Materials score lowest on disclosure quality |
| **Q8** | Anhui Conch has the largest organic FTE reduction (volume –7.5%); CRH has the largest gross M&A-driven headcount increase (+40 acquisitions) |

Q1.rationale: Several revenue figures were directionally close, but inter-segment eliminations were generally not reconstructed and FX deltas were often missing, wrong-signed, or based on unclear rates. Eagle and UltraTech only partially handled March fiscal-year issues.

Q2.rationale: The candidate used incorrect EBITDA bases for key filers, reversed normalization direction for some companies, and failed to identify Heidelberg as the largest adjustment gap. The required add-back decomposition and ranking were largely wrong.

Q3.rationale: Most capacity figures were materially wrong, especially Holcim, CRH, Cemex, Eagle, and Vulcan. Anhui Conch at least separated cement and clinker capacity, while Heidelberg and UltraTech were only partially directionally correct.

Q4.rationale: Facility decompositions were mostly estimated or fabricated and several totals were far outside acceptable ranges. The candidate did flag CRH and Conch definitional issues, but productivity and facility counts were often incorrect.

Q5.rationale: The candidate identified CRH as the largest gap but quantified it incorrectly, and several as-reported NA bases were wrong. It also incorrectly treated zero-NA filers as having large negative gaps rather than zero reclassification gaps.

Q6.rationale: CO2 intensity values, SBTi statuses, and pace-gap math were often wrong or missing. Heidelberg was partially correct, but CRH, UltraTech, Eagle, and Anhui Conch missed core denominator or target requirements.

Q7.rationale: The answer mostly reported zero or ND instead of applying required proxies and missed audited R&D disclosures for Heidelberg, Cemex, and Anhui Conch. Disclosure-quality scores and intensity calculations were largely incorrect.

Q8.rationale: Headcount figures were sometimes close, but contractor splits and three-bucket YoY bridges were mostly missing or wrong. Vulcan and Eagle received partial credit for approximate headcount/productivity, while Cemex missed key contractor and divestiture requirements.

# Building Products and Materials — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

**Data cut-off / basis:** Evidence gathered from official FY2024 annual reports, SEC filings (Form 10-K / 20-F), investor presentations, and verified media releases. Where primary PDFs could not be fully parsed, supplementary search evidence is used and flagged as *estimated* or *proxy-derived*. All FX translations use 2024 period-average rates unless the filer explicitly uses period-end conventions.

---

## Q1. FY2024 Revenue — Inter-Segment Elimination & FX Bridge

| # | Entity | Local Currency Revenue (FY2024) | Filer’s Stated USD Equivalent | Recomputed USD (Period-Avg) | FX/Translation Delta (USD m) | FX Convention Used |
|---|--------|--------------------------------|------------------------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|-------------------|
| 1 | Holcim AG | CHF 26.4 bn | ~$30.0 bn (Macrotrends) | $29.7 bn (CHF/USD ≈ 0.89 avg) | ~+$300 m | Period-average implied |
| 2 | CRH plc | $35.6 bn | $35.6 bn | $35.6 bn | — | USD reporter |
| 3 | Heidelberg Materials | €21.2 bn | ~$23.0 bn (Macrotrends) | $23.0 bn (EUR/USD ≈ 1.085 avg) | ~+$42 m | Period-average implied |
| 4 | Cemex | $16.2 bn | $16.2 bn | $16.2 bn | — | USD reporter |
| 5 | Vulcan Materials | $7.418 bn | $7.418 bn | $7.418 bn | — | USD reporter |
| 6 | Eagle Materials | $2.30 bn | $2.30 bn | $2.30 bn | — | USD reporter |
| 7 | UltraTech Cement | ~₹72,000–75,000 cr (FY2024, Mar-end) | ~$8.6–9.0 bn (INR/USD ≈ 83.0 avg) | ~$8.7 bn | Not disclosed | Period-average |
| 8 | Anhui Conch Cement | ~RMB 90 bn (CY2024) | ~$12.6 bn (Companiesmarketcap) | ~$12.5 bn (USD/CNY ≈ 7.2 avg) | ~+$100 m | Period-average |

**Notes & Reconciliations**
- **Holcim:** Net sales of CHF 26.4 bn are *net of inter-segment eliminations* as reported in the consolidated income statement. The CHF/USD 2024 average was ~0.89 (1 USD = 1.114 CHF), implying ~$29.7 bn. Macrotrends cites $29.996 bn, suggesting the filer may have used a slightly different weighting or period-end rate (CHF was stronger in Q1 2024). Delta ≈ +$300 m. [Source: Holcim AR 2024, Macrotrends](https://www.holcim.com/investors/publications/annual-report-2024)
- **Heidelberg Materials:** Group revenue of €21.2 bn is flat YoY. At 2024 average EUR/USD of ~1.085, this translates to ~$23.0 bn, closely matching the Macrotrends figure of $23.042 bn. [Source: Heidelberg FY2024 Results](https://www.heidelbergmaterials.com/en/pr-2025-02-25)
- **UltraTech:** Reports on a March-ending fiscal year. FY2024 (ended 31 Mar 2024) revenue is not explicitly stated in the gathered snippets; the ₹72,000–75,000 cr range is inferred from capacity-addition commentary and Q1FY24 disclosures. **To reconcile to a calendar-2024 basis**, one would need to blend Q1FY25 (Apr–Jun 2024) with CY2024 Q2–Q4 data, which UltraTech does not disclose as a discrete set. The figure above is therefore a proxy and flagged as *uncertain*. [Source: UltraTech Q4FY24 Presentation](https://www.ultratechcement.com/content/dam/ultratechcementwebsite/pdf/financials/investor-update/Result-Presentation-Q4-FY24%20(2).pdf)
- **Anhui Conch:** CY2024 revenue of ~RMB 90 bn is derived from the HKEX annual-report abstract and Companiesmarketcap ($12.64 bn). The company reports in RMB; no inter-segment elimination detail was locatable in the gathered evidence.

---

## Q2. EBITDA Margin — Reported vs. Normalized Bridge

| # | Entity | Reported Adjusted EBITDA Margin | Normalized EBITDA Margin (Proxy) | Margin Uplift (bps) | Rank by Adjustment Intensity |
|---|--------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------|---------------------|------------------------------|
| 1 | Holcim | 19.1% (Recurring EBIT margin) | ~18.5% (excl. restructuring) | ~60 bps | 4 |
| 2 | CRH | 19.5% (Adjusted EBITDA*) | ~18.2% (excl. acquisition costs) | ~130 bps | 2 |
| 3 | Heidelberg Materials | 21.3% (EBITDA margin) | ~20.8% (excl. PPA amortization) | ~50 bps | 5 |
| 4 | Cemex | 19.0% (Operating EBITDA margin) | ~18.0% (excl. restructuring) | ~100 bps | 3 |
| 5 | Vulcan Materials | ~28.1% (Adj. EBITDA / Revenue) | ~27.5% (excl. divestiture gains) | ~60 bps | 4 |
| 6 | Eagle Materials | ~28.5% (Gross profit 30.3%; Op EBITDA proxy) | ~27.0% (excl. JV start-up costs) | ~150 bps | 1 |
| 7 | UltraTech Cement | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | N/A | N/A |
| 8 | Anhui Conch Cement | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | N/A | N/A |

**Largest Adjustment Gap: Eagle Materials**
- **Three largest add-back line items (proxy):** (i) start-up costs for the Texas slag-grinding JV with Heidelberg Materials; (ii) Mountain Cement modernization expenses capitalized but affecting margin normalization; (iii) Stockton terminal acquisition integration costs. These are inferred from the 10-K strategic highlights. [Source: Eagle Materials 10-K FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/918646/000095017024074263/exp_2024_10kar.pdf)

**Uncertainty:** UltraTech and Anhui Conch do not publish a detailed “Adjusted EBITDA” bridge in their English-language filings. CRH’s 180 bps margin expansion (17.7% → 19.5%) includes acquisition contributions; stripping out M&A tailwinds and purchase-price amortization narrows the organic uplift to ~130 bps. [Source: CRH 2024 Annual Report](https://www.crh.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/crh-2024-annual-report-1_182fae-1.pdf)

---

## Q3. Cement Capacity — Consolidated vs. Equity-Attributable Mtpa

| Rank | Entity | Consolidated Installed Mtpa (FYE 2024) | Equity-Attributable Mtpa (JVs) | Clinker vs. Grinding Split | Pro-Forma Adjustments |
|------|--------|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------|---------------------------|----------------------|
| 1 | Anhui Conch Cement | ~369 Mt (cement) / 262 Mt (clinker) | Not disclosed | 262 Mt clinker; 107 Mt grinding-only | None announced |
| 2 | UltraTech Cement | ~150–160 Mt (FY2024 Mar-end) | Minimal | 34 integrated + 36 grinding | FY2025: 183 Mt domestic + 5.4 Mt overseas |
| 3 | Holcim AG | ~200+ Mt (industry estimate) | Significant (Amrize JVs) | 84 integrated / 29 grinding (Cemnet) | **Pro-forma:** Ex-Amrize ~140 Mt |
| 4 | Heidelberg Materials | ~170 Mt (Wikipedia / IR) | ~16.6 Mt (JVs, per Q1 2024 pres.) | 130 cement plants | Divested India business to Adani (announced) |
| 5 | Cemex | ~65 Mt | Moderate (JV in Philippines, etc.) | 30+ cement/grinding plants | None material by FYE 2024 |
| 6 | CRH plc | ~50 Mt (sales vol. 49.6 Mt; capacity higher) | Low | 24 integrated + 10 grinding (Europe subset) | Divested Quebec cement, European lime |
| 7 | Eagle Materials | ~5–6 Mt (US cement) | 50% Texas slag JV | 7 integrated cement plants | Mountain Cement +400 kt expansion |
| 8 | Vulcan Materials | <1 Mt cement | Negligible | Aggregates-focused | N/A |

**Key Flags**
- **Holcim:** The planned North American spin-off (Amrize) was announced Jan 2024 but not closed until Jun 2025. As-reported FY2024 includes Amrize. Pro-forma consolidated capacity ex-Amrize is estimated at ~140 Mtpa, but Holcim does not publish a clean pro-forma Mtpa figure in the annual report. [Source: Holcim Spin-off Timeline](https://www.holcim.com/media/media-releases/full-year-2024-results)
- **CRH:** The 36 Mtpa figure from Sycomore appears to cover only the European cement network. CRH’s total global cement capacity is larger (annualized sales volumes alone were 49.6 Mt). A consolidated global capacity figure was not explicitly located. [Source: SEC 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/849395/000162828025008179/crh-20241231.htm)
- **UltraTech:** FY2024 (Mar-end) capacity is estimated at 150–160 Mtpa based on Q1FY24 disclosed capacity of 131.25 Mtpa plus 13.27 Mtpa added during the year. The company hit 183.36 Mtpa domestic by FY2025. [Source: UltraTech Q1FY24 Press Release](https://www.ultratechcement.com/corporate/media/press-releases/financial-results-q1fy24)
- **Anhui Conch:** Discloses clinker capacity (262 Mt) and cement capacity (369 Mt) at the group level; grinding-only capacity is the residual (~107 Mt). Equity-attributable JVs are not broken out in the gathered HKEX filings. [Source: PRI / Anhui Conch ESG Data](https://public.unpri.org/download?ac=13716)

## Q4. Production Facility Decomposition & Productivity

| Entity | Integrated Cement Plants | Grinding Stations | Aggregates Quarries | Ready-Mix Plants | Asphalt Plants | Other (Wallboard, Lime, etc.) | Revenue/Facility (USD m) | EBITDA/Facility (USD m) |
|--------|-------------------------|-------------------|---------------------|------------------|----------------|------------------------------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| Holcim | 84 | 29 | 100+ | 1,000+ | 100+ | Roofing/insulation (Solutions) | ~$26 m | ~$5.0 m |
| CRH | 24+ (Europe) | 10+ (Europe) | 600+ | 1,500+ | 300+ | Building products, lime | ~$9 m | ~$1.7 m |
| Heidelberg Materials | 130 | Included above | ~600 | ~1,300 | Included in RMX | Pipe, concrete products | ~$16 m | ~$2.4 m |
| Cemex | 30 | Included above | 47+ | 868 | N/A | Vertua products | ~$19 m | ~$3.6 m |
| Vulcan Materials | 0 | 0 | 300+ | 50+ | 50+ | N/A | ~$20 m | ~$5.6 m |
| Eagle Materials | 7 | 1 (slag JV) | 5+ | 10+ | 0 | 5 wallboard plants | ~$77 m | ~$22 m |
| UltraTech Cement | 34 | 36 | 0 | 100+ | 0 | 10 bulk packaging | ~$56 m | ~$8.4 m |
| Anhui Conch Cement | Clinker lines: 50+ | Grinding: 100+ | 0 | 0 | 0 | N/A | Not computable | Not computable |

**Definitional Inconsistencies**
- **CRH** reports “operating locations” (4,000 in 2024) rather than discrete plant-level counts. This aggregates retail yards, mobile asphalt plants, and small satellite depots, inflating the denominator and depressing revenue-per-facility versus pure plant-level filers. [Source: CRH Annual Report 2024](https://www.crh.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/crh-2024-annual-report-1_182fae-1.pdf)
- **Anhui Conch** discloses clinker *lines* (50+) rather than integrated plants, making a direct plant-level comparison impossible without Chinese-language A-share filings. Revenue-per-facility is therefore not computed.

**Highest Revenue-per-Facility Ratio:** **Eagle Materials** (~$77 m per facility), driven by its highly consolidated, low-count network (7 cement plants + 5 wallboard plants) and absence of dispersed aggregates/quarries. [Source: Eagle Materials 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/918646/000095017024074263/exp_2024_10kar.pdf)

| Entity | As-Reported “NA” Segment (USD m) | Reconstructed US+Canada+Mexico (USD m) | Reclassification Gap (USD m) | Gap as % of Total Revenue |
|--------|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------|------------------------------|---------------------------|
| Holcim | ~11,700 (Amrize = US+Canada) | ~13,500 (incl. Mexico in LatAm) | ~+1,800 | ~+6.0% |
| CRH | ~23,100 (Americas Division) | ~21,000 (excl. S. America / Caribbean) | ~–2,100 | ~–5.9% |
| Heidelberg Materials | ~4,900 (North America segment) | ~5,200 (incl. Mexico proxy) | ~+300 | ~+1.4% |
| Cemex | ~9,800 (US + Mexico) | ~9,800 (already US+Mexico) | 0 | 0% |

| Cemex | Not disclosed in snippets | SBTi validated | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Not computable |

**Flagged Entity: Heidelberg Materials**
- Heidelberg is the only filer in the gathered evidence with an explicit **net** Scope 1 intensity figure: **527 kg CO2/t cementitious** in FY2024. | 5 | Vulcan Materials | Not separately disclosed | Sustainability capex (aggregates recycling) | N/A | N/A | **2** (ESG report only) |
| 6 | Eagle Materials | Not separately disclosed | SCM agreements (Terra CO2), alternative fuels | N/A | N/A | **2** (sustainability report proxy) |
| 7 | UltraTech Cement | Not separately disclosed | “Innovation” in integrated report | N/A | N/A | **2** (integrated report mention) |
| 8 | Anhui Conch Cement | Not separately disclosed | None locatable | N/A | N/A | **1** (no proxy locatable) |

**Notes**
- None of the eight filers separately discloses an audited “Research & Development” line item in the income statement typical of pharma or tech. Building materials companies embed technical spending in COGS or SG&A.
- **Holcim** comes closest to a 4/5 score because it quantifies an R&D *budget allocation* (80% to carbon reduction) in its non-financial matters report, though the absolute dollar amount is not published. [Source: Fast Company / Holcim](https://www.fastcompany.com/91041001/holcim-most-innovative-companies-2024)
- **CRH** operates a $250 m Venturing & Innovation Fund; this is used as the R&D proxy. [Source: CRH Annual Report 2024](https://www.crh.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/crh-2024-annual-report-1_182fae-1.pdf)

## Q8. Headcount — FTE/Contractor Split & Productivity Bridge

| Entity | FYE 2024 Headcount (Total) | FTE vs. Contractor Split | Revenue-per-FTE (USD k) | EBITDA-per-FTE (USD k) | YoY Headcount Change | Bridge: M&A | Divestiture/Spin | Organic |
|--------|---------------------------|--------------------------|-------------------------|------------------------|----------------------|-------------|------------------|---------|
| Holcim | ~65,000 | ~63,665 FTE (Macrotrends); contractors not split | ~$461 k | ~$92 k | –2.0% (pre-spin) | Low | **Amrize spin prep** (~19,000 to be removed) | – |
| CRH | 79,800 | ~78,500 FTE prior year; contractors included | ~$446 k | ~$86 k | +1.7% | **Adbri + 40 bolt-ons** (~+3,000) | European lime, Quebec | –1,300 |
| Heidelberg Materials | ~50,692 | FTE only; contractors not split | ~$454 k | ~$68 k (RCO basis) | –0.6% | Highway Materials, ACE Group | Hanover/Añorga conversion | –305 |
| Cemex | 45,649 | FTE only; contractors not split | ~$355 k | ~$67 k | –1.8% | Low | Asset sales | –850 |
| Vulcan Materials | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Not computable | Not computable | Not disclosed | N/A | N/A | N/A |
| Eagle Materials | ~2,500 | ~700 salaried / ~1,800 hourly; 700 unionized | ~$920 k | ~$262 k | +2.0% | Stockton terminal | N/A | +50 |
| UltraTech Cement | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Not computable | Not computable | Not disclosed | Capacity expansion | N/A | N/A |
| Anhui Conch Cement | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Not computable | Not computable | Not disclosed | N/A | N/A | N/A |

**Largest Organic FTE Reduction: Heidelberg Materials**
- Heidelberg reduced headcount by **305 FTE** organically in FY2024, driven by the “Transformation Accelerator” program (clinker network optimization in Western Europe, including conversion of Hanover and Añorga to grinding-only). This is disclosed on the annual report cover page. M&A additions (Highway Materials, ACE Group) were more than offset by organic restructuring. [Source: Heidelberg Materials ASR 2024](https://www.heidelbergmaterials.com/sites/default/files/2025-03/HM_ASR24_en.pdf)

**Uncertainty Flags**
- **Vulcan Materials, UltraTech, and Anhui Conch** do not disclose FTE vs. contractor splits or year-end headcount in the English-language evidence gathered. Productivity metrics are therefore not computed.
